speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the number and percentage of social visit pass holders from China who have been arrested has increased since the 30-day visa exemption arrangement became effective on 9 February 2024; and (b) whether the ability of all foreigners to enter via automated lanes at Changi Airport without presenting themselves before an immigration officer since May 2024 has increased the risk of persons who are not bona fide travellers entering Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police had previously provided a comprehensive update on this issue.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Another 14 Chinese nationals are of interest to the Police, but they remain overseas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: A visa regime is not a foolproof way to keep unwanted characters away.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It enables us to pre-screen individuals before they travel to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: If they have antecedents of concern, their visa application will be rejected.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The need to apply for a visa and to submit supporting documentation also acts as a deterrence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: But no visa regime will completely weed out undesirable visitors and neither will it stop them from committing crimes here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) adopts a risk-based, multi-layered approach to assess a foreign traveller when he is at our checkpoints.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Over the years, the systems have been upgraded, the checks have become more robust and the overall level of security has been enhanced.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It may surprise Mr Leong to know that the percentage of travellers who are refused entry into Singapore has, in fact, increased with ICA's new clearance concept and automated clearance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Because checks are now further upstream and we leverage technology even more extensively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Pre-arrival, ICA uses advanced passenger information, including flight manifests and information from the SG Arrival Card, to conduct data analytics and a risk assessment of travellers through its Integrated Targeting Centre.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Upon arrival, all travellers, including those at the automated lanes, are screened against a watchlist of persons of interest as well as those who have been flagged by ICA's Integrated Targeting Centre to be of higher risk.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Such individuals are stopped for more stringent immigration and security checks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Repeat travellers, including those who had committed crimes in Singapore, who try to enter via a different identity, will be flagged by our biometric database because we would have captured their biometrics on their previous visit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Because we have automated more processes, more ICA officers can be deployed to conduct profiling of travellers at the automated immigration lanes, which complements the back-end risk assessment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Those spotted to be exhibiting suspicious behaviour will be sieved out for questioning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Mr Leong's questions may have been prompted by fears of foreigners committing crimes in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The only way we can be sure that foreigners will not commit crimes here is to close our borders to them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Singapore and Singaporeans benefit from the tourism revenue and employment opportunities that foreigners, including those from China, bring.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The sector also contributed, on average, 3% of Singapore's gross domestic product (GDP) over the last 10 years, from 2014 to 2023, excluding 2020 to 2022 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In addition to being an important economic contributor, tourism plays an essential role in reinforcing Singapore's status as a vibrant global city that is a magnet for capital, businesses and talent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It also enhances the quality and diversity of leisure options for local residents and helps to create a living environment that Singaporeans can be proud to call home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There is no way to realise these ambitions if we erect walls and keep visitors out.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Our neighbours, Malaysia and Thailand, have also rolled out initiatives to boost tourism.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For instance, to attract Chinese visitors, they have implemented visa exemption, increased flight frequencies and promoted cultural and entertainment experiences that appeal to Chinese travellers.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But first of all, I would like to stress that neither I nor the Progress Singapore Party (PSP) have ever advocated for a closed Singapore.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We understand the benefits of an open society and open economy.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But as the number of foreigners or foreign visitors increase over time, I think we will need additional measures to protect the security of our country and our society.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Given that some of the Chinese nationals have come to Singapore and committed crimes, like scams, money laundering and, now, even burglaries, is the Government considering tougher penalties on these cross-border criminal activities?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think we need to, in addition to all the measures that the Minister of State had explained just now, also increase the deterrent on people coming to Singapore and committing crimes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On transnational crime, there are various aspects to it.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There is human trafficking, drug trafficking; there are online scams.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Burglary is not exactly a transnational crime, but I think when Mr Leong referred to it, he meant it in terms of foreigners who may come to Singapore to commit such crimes.
